117055.subject: Chemistry
117055.text:
Consider the following statements regarding d-block elements:
(I) Chromium has the maximum number of unpaired electrons in its ground state among the $3\text{d}$ series elements.
(II) The highest oxidation state shown by any transition element is $+8$, which is exhibited by Osmium.
(III) Copper is the only metal in the $3\text{d}$ series with a positive standard reduction potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{M}^{2+}/\text{M}}$).
(IV) Zinc, Cadmium, and Mercury are hard metals with high melting points due to strong metallic bonding.

How many of the above statements are correct?
117055.sol:
Statement (I) is correct: Chromium has the electronic configuration $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^{5} 4\text{s}^{1}$, giving it $6$ unpaired electrons, which is the maximum in the $3\text{d}$ series.

Statement (II) is correct: Osmium (and Ruthenium) can exhibit an oxidation state of $+8$, the highest among transition elements.

Statement (III) is correct: Copper has a positive standard reduction potential ($E^{\circ}_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} = +0.34\text{ V}$), while all other $3\text{d}$ series metals have negative values.

Statement (IV) is incorrect: Zinc, Cadmium, and Mercury have completely filled d-orbitals which do not participate in metallic bonding. Consequently, they have weak metallic bonds, making them soft metals with low melting points.

Therefore, exactly $3$ statements are correct.

Answer: $3$

117787.text:
Given below are four statements regarding coordination compounds:
(I) The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$ exhibits both geometrical and optical isomerism.
(II) Facial (fac) and meridional (mer) isomers are shown by octahedral complexes of type $\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3$.
(III) The complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$ is optically active.
(IV) Linkage isomerism arises in coordination compounds containing ambidentate ligands.

How many of the above statements are correct?
117787.sol:
Statement (I) is incorrect: The complex $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]^+$ is an octahedral complex of type $\text{MA}_4\text{B}_2$. It exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms), but both forms possess a plane of symmetry and are optically inactive.

Statement (II) is correct: Octahedral complexes of the type $\text{MA}_3\text{B}_3$ (e.g., $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3(\text{NO}_2)_3]$) exhibit facial (fac) and meridional (mer) geometrical isomerism.

Statement (III) is incorrect: Platinum(II) forms square planar complexes. The complex $[\text{Pt}(\text{en})_2]^{2+}$ has a square planar geometry, which contains a plane of symmetry. Hence, it is achiral and optically inactive.

Statement (IV) is correct: Linkage isomerism occurs in coordination compounds that contain ambidentate ligands (like $\text{NO}_2^-$, $\text{SCN}^-$), which can bind to the central metal atom through more than one donor atom.

Thus, only two statements (II and IV) are correct.

Answer: Only two

Reaction 1: Treatment with $HBr$ yields major product A.

Identify the IUPAC names of products A and B.
118800.sol:
Reaction 1 (with $HBr$): The reaction proceeds via a carbocation intermediate. Protonation and loss of water from 3-methylpentan-2-ol forms a secondary carbocation at C-2. A 1,2-hydride shift occurs from C-3 to C-2 to form a more stable tertiary carbocation. Nucleophilic attack by $Br^-$ yields 3-bromo-3-methylpentane as the major product (A).

Reaction 2 (with $SOCl_2$): The reaction of alcohols with thionyl chloride ($SOCl_2$) follows an $S_Ni$ (or $S_N2$ in the presence of a base) mechanism. This mechanism does not involve a free carbocation intermediate, so no carbocation rearrangement occurs. The $-OH$ group is directly replaced by $-Cl$ at the same position, yielding 2-chloro-3-methylpentane as the major product (B).

Answer: A = 3-bromo-3-methylpentane, B = 2-chloro-3-methylpentane

Semicarbazide has two amino (NH<sub>2</sub>) groups, out of which one is involved in resonance as shown above. Electron-density on this (NH<sub>2</sub>) decreases and it does not act as a nucleophile.   But the other (NH<sub>2</sub>) group (attached to NH) has a lone pair of electrons which are not involved in resonance. Semicarbazide can undergo tautomerization in solution, leading to the selective participation of one -NH<sub>2</sub>group in semicarbazone formation.

Correct Option is : (B)

But the other (NH2) group (attached to NH) has a lone pair of electrons which are not involved in resonance. So, this pair is available for the nucleophilic attack on the carbonyl group (>C=O) of aldehydes and/or ketones.

121313.text: What are the bodies of fungi made of?
options: Long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae
121313.sol: With the exception of yeasts which are unicellular, fungi are filamentous. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Their bodies consist of long, slender thread-like structures called hyphae</mark>. The network of hyphae is known as mycelium. Some hyphae are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm – these are called coenocytic hyphae. Others have septae or cross walls in their hyphae. The cell walls of fungi are composed of chitin and polysaccharides.

121709.subject: Botany
121709.text: How do algae affect the level of dissolved oxygen in their environment?
121709.sol: Algae are useful to man in a variety of ways. At least a half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by algae through photosynthesis. <mark>Being photosynthetic they increase the level of dissolved oxygen in their immediate environment.</mark> They are of paramount importance as primary producers of energy-rich compounds which form the basis of the food cycles of all aquatic animals. Many species of Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are among the 70 species of marine algae used as food. Certain marine brown and red algae produce large amounts of hydrocolloids (water holding substances), e.g., algin (brown algae) and carrageenan (red algae) which are used commercially. Agar, one of the commercial products obtained from Gelidium and Gracilaria, are used to grow microbes and in preparations of ice-creams and jellies. Chlorella, a unicellular alga rich in proteins, is used as a food supplement even by space travelers. The algae are divided into three main classes: Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae and Rhodophyceae.

121823.subject: Botany
121823.text: Which genera produce two kinds of spores in Pteridophytes?
121823.sol: Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes. In the majority of the pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds; such plants are called homosporous. <mark>Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro (large) and micro (small) spores, are known as heterosporous.</mark> The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is a precursor to the seed habit considered an important step in evolution. The pteridophytes are further classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum).

123046.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Flowers of Cassia and Gulmohur exhibit imbricate aestivation.
Reason (R): In these flowers, one margin of the appendage overlaps that of the next one and so on in a particular direction.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
123046.sol:
Assertion (A) is correct. Cassia and Gulmohur are classic examples of flowers exhibiting imbricate aestivation.

Reason (R) is incorrect. In imbricate aestivation, the margins of sepals or petals overlap one another but not in any particular direction. The description given in the Reason (overlapping in a particular direction) corresponds to twisted aestivation, not imbricate.

Therefore, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

123719.subject: Botany
123719.text: What is the process by which cells arise from preexisting cells according to the cell theory?
123719.sol: According to the cell theory, cells arise from preexisting cells. The process by which this occurs is called cell division. Any sexually reproducing organism starts its life cycle from a single-celled zygote. Cell division does not stop with the formation of the mature organism but continues throughout its life cycle. The stages through which a cell passes from one division to the next is called the cell cycle. Cell cycle is divided into two phases called (i) Interphase – a period of preparation for cell division, and (ii) Mitosis (M phase) – the actual period of cell division.

123810.subject: Botany
123810.text: A cell at the $G_{1}$ phase of its cell cycle has 14 chromosomes and 20 pg of DNA. What will be the number of chromosomes and the amount of DNA in the same cell at the $G_{2}$ phase?
123810.sol:
During the cell cycle, the $G_{1}$ phase is followed by the S phase and then the $G_{2}$ phase.

In the S (synthesis) phase, DNA replication occurs. As a result, the amount of DNA per cell doubles. Therefore, the initial 20 pg of DNA in the $G_{1}$ phase will become 40 pg by the $G_{2}$ phase.

However, during the S phase, there is no increase in the chromosome number because the newly synthesized sister chromatids remain attached at the same centromere. Thus, the cell will still have 14 chromosomes in the $G_{2}$ phase.

Hence, the cell at the $G_{2}$ phase will have 14 chromosomes and 40 pg of DNA.

Answer: 14 chromosomes and 40 pg of DNA

123839.subject: Botany
123839.text:
Read the following statements carefully:
(i) Initiation of the assembly of mitotic spindle occurs in prophase.
(ii) Cells at the end of prophase, when viewed under the microscope, do not show Golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus and the nuclear envelope.
(iii) In telophase, chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements.
(iv) During anaphase, the centromere of each chromosome is directed towards the equator while the arms trail behind.

How many of the above statements are correct?
123839.sol:
Statement (i) is correct as the initiation of the assembly of the mitotic spindle is a characteristic event of prophase.

Statement (ii) is correct because by the end of prophase, organelles like the Golgi complexes, endoplasmic reticulum, nucleolus, and the nuclear envelope disappear.

Statement (iii) is correct as telophase is marked by the decondensation of chromosomes at opposite poles, where they lose their individuality and discrete identity.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. During anaphase, as the chromosomes move away from the equatorial plate, the centromere of each chromosome is directed towards the pole (leading edge), while the arms trail behind.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

124309.subject: Botany
124309.text: A dense, granular cell organelle was first observed by George Palade under the electron microscope in 1953. Which of the following statements correctly describes the nature of this organelle?
options: It is composed of ribonucleic acid and proteins and is not surrounded by any membrane.
It is a single membrane-bound vesicular structure rich in various hydrolytic enzymes.
It consists of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae stacked parallel to each other.
It is an endomembrane structure which acts as a major site for the synthesis of lipids.
124309.sol:
The granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953) are ribosomes.

Ribosomes are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane.

The other options describe lysosomes (vesicular structures with hydrolytic enzymes), Golgi apparatus (flat, disc-shaped sacs), and smooth endoplasmic reticulum (major site for lipid synthesis).

Answer: It is composed of ribonucleic acid and proteins and is not surrounded by any membrane.

128286.subject: Zoology
128286.text: What hormone regulates the growth of the mammary glands and the formation of milk?
128286.sol: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications, and premature death if unchecked. The disease is hard to diagnose in the early stages and often goes undetected for many years, until changes in external features become noticeable. Prolactin regulates the growth of the mammary glands and formation of milk in them. TSH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of thyroid hormones from the thyroid gland. ACTH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of steroid hormones called glucocorticoids from the adrenal cortex. LH and FSH stimulate gonadal activity and hence are called gonadotrophins. In males, LH stimulates the synthesis and secretion of hormones called androgens from testis. In males, FSH and androgens regulate spermatogenesis. In females, LH induces ovulation of fully mature follicles (graafian follicles) and maintains the corpus luteum, formed from the remnants of the graafian follicles after ovulation.

129502.subject: Zoology
129502.text: What is the name of the vessel that runs parallel to the Henle's loop?
129502.sol: The Malpighian corpuscle, PCT and DCT of the nephron are situated in the cortical region of the kidney whereas the loop of Henle dips into the medulla. In majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla. Such nephrons are called cortical nephrons. In some of the nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla. These nephrons are called juxta medullary nephrons. The efferent arteriole emerging from the glomerulus forms a fine capillary network around the renal tubule called the peritubular capillaries. A minute vessel of this network runs parallel to the Henle’s loop forming a ‘U’ shaped vasa recta. Vasa recta is absent or highly reduced in cortical nephrons.

130572.subject: Zoology
130572.text: What additional benefit do condoms provide besides contraception?
130572.sol: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that are used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. This can prevent conception. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condom for the male. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. Both the male and the female condoms are disposable, can be self-inserted and thereby gives privacy to the user. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix. They are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used alongwith these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency.

130617.subject: Zoology
130617.text: Which age group has a very high incidence of STDs?
130617.sol: STIs are a major threat to a healthy society. Therefore, prevention or early detection and cure of these diseases are given prime consideration under the Reproductive Health-care programmes. Though all persons are vulnerable to these infections, their incidences are reported to be very high among persons in the age group of 15-24 years – the age group to which you also belong. There is no reason to panic because prevention is possible. One could be free of these infections by following the simple principles given below: (i) Avoid sex with unknown partners/multiple partners. (ii) Always try to use condoms during coitus. (iii) In case of doubt, one should go to a qualified doctor for early detection and get complete treatment if diagnosed with infection.

130819.subject: Zoology
130819.text: What is the first event in Human Reproduction?
130819.sol: Humans are sexually reproducing and viviparous. The reproductive events in humans include formation of gametes (gametogenesis), i.e., sperms in males and ovum in females, transfer of sperms into the female genital tract (insemination) and fusion of male and female gametes (fertilisation) leading t formation of zygote. This is followed by formation and development of blastocyst and its attachment to the uterine wall (implantation), embryonic development (gestation) and delivery of the baby (parturition). You have learnt that these reproductive events occur after puberty. There are remarkable differences between the reproductive events in the male and in the female, for example, sperm formation continues even in old men, but formation of ovum ceases in women around the age of fifty years.

In a hypothetical transcription unit, the coding strand of DNA has the following sequence:

$5'$-TACGTAGC-$3'$

What will be the sequence of the transcribed mRNA, and at which end of this coding strand is the terminator located?
131890.sol:
By convention, the sequence of the transcribed mRNA is identical to the coding strand of DNA, with the only exception being that Thymine (T) is replaced by Uracil (U) in RNA.

Given coding strand: $5'$-TACGTAGC-$3'$
Transcribed mRNA: $5'$-UACGUAGC-$3'$

Furthermore, all reference points while defining a transcription unit are made with respect to the coding strand. The terminator is located towards the $3'$ end (downstream) of the coding strand, which defines the end of the transcription process.

Answer: mRNA: $5'$-UACGUAGC-$3'$ ; Terminator: $3'$ end

132180.subject: Zoology
132180.text: How did Mendel's approach differ from that of other biologists of his time?
options: He used chemistry to explain biological phenomena
He used mathematics to explain biological phenomena
He used physics to explain biological phenomena
He used philosophy to explain biological phenomena
132180.sol: Mendel published his work on inheritance of characters in 1865 but for several reasons, it remained unrecognized till 1900. Firstly, communication was not easy (as it is now) in those days and his work could not be widely publicized. Secondly, his concept of genes (or factors, in Mendel’s words) as stable and discrete units that controlled the expression of traits and, of the pair of alleles which did not ‘blend’ with each other, was not accepted by his contemporaries as an explanation for the apparently continuous variation seen in nature. Thirdly, Mendel’s approach of using mathematics to explain biological phenomena was totally new and unacceptable to many of the biologists of his time. Finally, though Mendel’s work suggested that factors (genes) were discrete units, he could not provide any physical proof for the existence of factors or say what they were made of.
132180.meta: How did Mendel's approach differ from that of other biologists of his time?

Convergent evolution occurs in unrelated group of organisms. It is the development of similar functional structures but in unrelated groups.
The process of evolution of different species in a given geographical area starting from a point and literally radiating to other areas of geography is called adaptive radiation. Natural selection is the basis of evolution.

133262.sol: AIDS stands for Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, which means a deficiency of the immune system acquired during the lifetime of an individual indicating that it is not a congenital disease. Macrophages continue to produce virus particles and act as a factory for producing HIV.ue to the replication of HIV in helper T-lymphocytes, there is a progressive decrease in the number of helper T-lymphocytes in the body of the infected person.HIV is transmitted through body fluids such as sexual contact with an infected person, transfusion of contaminated blood and blood products, sharing of infected needles, and from an infected mother to her child through the placenta. People who are at high risk of getting HIV infection include individuals with multiple sexual partners, drug addicts who take drugs intravenously, individuals who require repeated blood transfusions, and children born to an HIV-infected mother.

134876.subject: Zoology
134876.text: In a continuous culture system, the used medium is drained out from one side while fresh medium is added from the other. Which specific phase of the microbial growth curve is maintained by this method to achieve maximum productivity?
134876.sol:
In a continuous culture system, the used medium is continuously drained out from one side while fresh medium is added from the other.

This constant replenishment of nutrients and removal of waste products prevents the depletion of resources and the accumulation of toxins.

As a result, the cells are maintained in their physiologically most active state, which is the log or exponential phase of the microbial growth curve, thereby achieving maximum productivity.

The lag phase is the initial adaptation period, the stationary phase occurs when nutrients are depleted, and the decline phase is when cell death exceeds division.

Answer: Exponential phase

135400.subject: Zoology
135400.text:
Read the following statements regarding the pollination mechanism in the Mediterranean orchid Ophrys:

(A) It offers nectar as a floral reward to its pollinator.
(B) One petal of its flower bears an uncanny resemblance to the female bee in size, colour, and markings.
(C) It relies on pseudocopulation by the male bee for pollen transfer.
(D) It exhibits co-evolution, as the orchid flower must co-evolve if the female bee's colour patterns change.

How many of the above statements are correct?
135400.sol:
Statement (A) is incorrect because the Mediterranean orchid Ophrys does not offer any floral rewards like nectar; instead, it employs sexual deceit.

Statement (B) is correct as one petal of its flower is modified to resemble the female bee in size, colour, and markings.

Statement (C) is correct because the male bee is attracted to the petal and 'pseudocopulates' with the flower, during which pollen is transferred.

Statement (D) is correct as this interaction is a classic example of co-evolution; the orchid must co-evolve to maintain the resemblance if the female bee's colour patterns change.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

303290.subject: Physics
303290.text:
Consider the arrangement illustrated in the figure. Suppose a small electric field $E$ acts in the vertically upward direction, and the upper block has a positive charge $Q$ on its top surface. The friction coefficient between the two blocks is $\mu$, while the floor is smooth. Determine the maximum horizontal force $F$ that can be applied without disturbing the equilibrium.
[Hint: The force exerted on a charge $Q$ by the electric field $E$ is $F = QE$ in the direction of $E$.]
303290.sol:
Let $N$ be the normal reaction between the upper block of mass $m$ and the lower block of mass $M$.

For the upper block, the forces in the vertical direction are its weight $mg$ acting downwards, the normal reaction $N$ acting upwards, and the electric force $F_e = QE$ acting upwards (since the charge is positive and the electric field is vertically upward).
For vertical equilibrium of the upper block:
$N + QE = mg$
$\Rightarrow N = mg - QE$

The maximum static friction force between the two blocks is:
$f_{\max} = \mu N = \mu(mg - QE)$

Let $T$ be the tension in the string. When the maximum horizontal force $F$ is applied to the left on the upper block, it tends to slide to the left relative to the lower block. Thus, the friction force $f$ on the upper block acts to the right.
For the horizontal equilibrium of the upper block:
$F = T + f$

For the lower block, the string pulls it to the right with tension $T$, and the friction force $f$ exerted by the upper block acts to the left. Since the floor is smooth, there is no friction from the floor.
For the horizontal equilibrium of the lower block:
$T = f$

Substituting $T = f$ into the equation for the upper block, we get:
$F = f + f = 2f$

To find the maximum force $F$ without disturbing the equilibrium, the friction must be at its limiting value, $f = f_{\max}$.
$F_{\max} = 2f_{\max} = 2\mu(mg - QE)$

303419.text: In a charging $R$–$C$ circuit, the electric current is given by $i = i_0 e^{-t/RC}$, where $i_0$, $R$, and $C$ are constant parameters of the circuit and $t$ represents time. Determine the rate of change of current at $t = 10 RC$.
303419.sol:
The electric current in the circuit is given by $i = i_0 e^{-t/RC}$.

The rate of change of current is obtained by differentiating $i$ with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt} \left( i_0 e^{-t/RC} \right) = i_0 e^{-t/RC} \left( -\dfrac{1}{RC} \right) = -\dfrac{i_0}{RC} e^{-t/RC}$

Substituting $t = 10RC$ into the expression:

$\dfrac{di}{dt} = -\dfrac{i_0}{RC} e^{-10RC/RC} = -\dfrac{i_0}{RC} e^{-10} = -\dfrac{i_0}{RCe^{10}}$

303925.subject: Physics
303925.text: A uniform rod, pivoted at its upper end, hangs vertically. It is displaced by an angle of $60^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ and subsequently released. Determine the magnitude of the force acting on a particle of mass $dm$ located at the tip of the rod when it forms an angle of $37^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the vertical.
303925.sol:
Let the mass of the uniform rod be $M and its length be $L$. The moment of inertia of the rod about the pivot is $I = \dfrac{ML^2}{3}$.

When the rod is at an angle $\theta = 37^\circ$ with the vertical, the torque about the pivot is provided by the weight of the rod acting at its center of mass:

$\tau = Mg \dfrac{L}{2} \sin 37^\circ$

Using $\tau = I\alpha$, the angular acceleration $\alpha$ is:

$\dfrac{ML^2}{3} \alpha = Mg \dfrac{L}{2} $\$left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)

$\alpha = $\dfrac{3g}{2L} \times \dfrac{3}{5} = \dfrac{9g}{10L} = \dfrac{0.9g}{L}

The tangential acceleration of the particle at the tip of the rod is:

$a_t = \alpha L = 0.9g$

To find the angular velocity $\omega$ at $\theta = 37^\circ$, we use the conservation of mechanical energy. The rod is released from rest at $\theta_0 = 60^\circ$. The decrease in potential energy is equal to the gain in kinetic energy:

$\Delta U = Mg $\dfrac{L}{2} (\cos$37^\circ - \cos 60^\circ) = $\dfrac{1}{2}$I \omega^2$

$Mg $\dfrac{L}{2} \left( \dfrac{4}{5} - \dfrac{1}{2} \right) = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{ML^2}{3} \right) \omega^2$

$Mg $\dfrac{L}{2} \left( \dfrac{3}{10} \right) = \dfrac{ML^2}{6} \omega^2$

\dfrac{3g}{20} = \dfrac{L}{6} \omega^2 \Rightarrow \omega^2 = $\dfrac{18g}{20L} = \dfrac{0.9g}{L}

The radial (centripetal) acceleration of the particle at the tip is:

$a_r = \omega^2 L = 0.9g$

The net acceleration of the particle of mass $dm$ is the vector sum of its tangential and radial accelerations:

$a = $\sqrt{a_t^2 + a_r^2} = \sqrt{(0.9g)^2 + (0.9g)^2} =$0.$9\sqrt{2}$g$

According to Newton's second law, the magnitude of the net force acting on the particle is:

$F = dm \times a = 0.$9\sqrt{2}$\,dm\,g$

Answer: $0.$9\sqrt{2}$\,dm\,g

304173.subject: Physics
304173.text: While riding a bicycle towards a vertical wall at $12 \text{ km h}^{-1}$, a boy whistles at his dog on the ground. Given that the whistle has a frequency of $1600 \text{ Hz}$ and the speed of sound in air is $330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, determine the frequency of the whistle as received by the wall.
304173.sol:
Speed of the source (boy on the bicycle), $v_s = 12 \text{ km h}^{-1} = 12 \times \dfrac{5}{18} \text{ m s}^{-1} = \dfrac{10}{3} \text{ m s}^{-1}$

Frequency of the source, $f = 1600 \text{ Hz}$

Speed of sound in air, $v = 330 \text{ m s}^{-1}$

The wall acts as a stationary observer while the source is moving towards it. Using the Doppler effect formula for a moving source and a stationary observer, the apparent frequency $f'$ received by the wall is given by:

$f' = f \left( \dfrac{v}{v - v_s} \right)

Substituting the given values:

$f' = 1600 \left( \dfrac{330}{330 - \dfrac{10}{3}} \right)$

$f' = 1600 \left( $\dfrac{330}{\dfrac{990 - 10}{3}} \right)

$f' = 1600 \left( $\dfrac{990}{980} \right)$

$f' = 1600 $\times $\dfrac{99}{98}$

$f' \approx1616.32 $\text{ Hz}

The closest frequency is $1616 $\text{ Hz}.

304548.subject: Physics
304548.text: Two bullets are fired simultaneously and horizontally from the same place, with different speeds. Which bullet will hit the ground first?
304548.sol:
The vertical motion of a projectile is independent of its horizontal motion.

For both bullets, the initial vertical velocity is zero ($u_y = 0$).

Using the equation of motion for the vertical direction, $h = u_y t + \dfrac{1}{2} g t^2$.

Since $u_y = 0$, the time taken to reach the ground is $t = \sqrt{\dfrac{2h}{g}}$.

As both bullets are fired from the same height $h$ and experience the same acceleration due to gravity $g$, the time of flight $t$ is the same for both.

Therefore, both bullets will reach the ground simultaneously.

304665.subject: Physics
304665.chapter: Wave Motion and Waves on a String
304665.text: Two wave pulses approach each other while travelling in opposite directions on a string. One pulse has a shape that is inverted relative to the other.
options: The pulses will pass through one another, although their shapes will be modified.
The pulses will reflect off one another, such that the rightward pulse will eventually move leftward and vice versa.
The pulses will pass through one another without experiencing any change in their shapes.
The pulses will collide and vanish entirely after the collision.
304665.sol:
According to the principle of superposition, when two wave pulses travelling in opposite directions overlap, the resultant displacement of the string is the algebraic sum of the individual displacements.

The waves do not interact in a way that permanently alters their properties. After the region of overlap, both wave pulses emerge and continue to travel in their original directions with their original shapes, amplitudes, and speeds completely unchanged.

Thus, the pulses pass through one another without experiencing any change in their shapes.

304724.subject: Physics
304724.text: A block rests on a rough floor while a horizontal force $F$ is exerted on it. The frictional force $f$ acting on the block due to the floor is recorded for various values of $F$, and a graph is plotted between the two variables.
options: There is a small kink present in the graph.
The graph is a straight line with a slope of $45^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$.
The graph is a straight line with a slope of $45^{}^{{}^{\circ}}$ for small $F$ and a straight line parallel to the $F$-axis for large $F$.
The graph is a straight line parallel to the $F$-axis.
304724.sol:
When the applied horizontal force $F$ is less than the limiting static friction, the block remains at rest. In this region, the static frictional force $f$ adjusts itself to be equal in magnitude to the applied force $F$. Thus, $f = F$, which represents a straight line passing through the origin with a slope of $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$.

When $F$ exceeds the limiting static friction $f_{s, max}$, the block begins to slide. The frictional force then becomes kinetic friction $f_{k}$. Since the coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu_{k}$ is generally slightly less than the coefficient of static friction $\mu_{s}$, the frictional force drops slightly from $f_{s, max}$ to $f_{k}$. This sudden drop appears as a small kink in the graph.

For all further increases in $F$ (large $F$), the kinetic friction remains constant at $f_{k}$, making the graph a straight line parallel to the $F$-axis.

Therefore, the graph has a slope of $45^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}}$ for small $F$, a small kink at the transition, and is parallel to the $F$-axis for large $F$.

304799.text: The properties of a surface differ from those of the bulk liquid because the surface molecules

304799.sol:
Molecules deep inside a liquid are surrounded by similar molecules on all sides, making the net intermolecular force on them zero.

Molecules at the surface are not completely surrounded by liquid molecules. They have liquid molecules below them and molecules of a different medium (like air or vapor) above them. Thus, they encounter different types of molecules within their range of influence.

Due to the difference in the number and type of molecules above and below, the cohesive downward force from the liquid is greater than the adhesive upward force from the medium above. As a result, surface molecules experience a net inward force (in one direction) towards the bulk of the liquid.

Therefore, surface molecules experience a net force in one direction and encounter different types of molecules within their range of influence.

304890.subject: Physics
304890.text: A particle remains at rest when observed from a certain frame. We can conclude that
options: the frame might be inertial, but the resultant force on the particle is zero
the resultant force acting on the particle is zero
the frame is an inertial frame
the frame might be noninertial, but there is a nonzero resultant force
304890.sol:
If a particle is at rest in a given frame of reference, its acceleration with respect to that frame is zero.

If the frame is an inertial frame, the acceleration of the particle with respect to the ground is zero. According to Newton's second law, the net real force acting on the particle must be zero.

If the frame is a non-inertial frame accelerating with $\vec{a}_0$ with respect to the ground, the particle must also have an acceleration $\vec{a}_0$ with respect to the ground to remain at rest in the non-inertial frame. Thus, the net real force acting on the particle is $m\vec{a}_0$, which is non-zero.

Therefore, the frame might be inertial with zero resultant force, or it might be non-inertial with a non-zero resultant force.

305118.subject: Physics
305118.text: Find the potential difference $V_a - V_b$ between nodes $a$ and $b$ for the circuit labeled (c) in the provided figure.
305118.sol:
In the circuit labeled (c), let the potential at the bottom middle node $b$ be $V_b = 0$.

The left battery has an electromotive force of $2 \text{ V}$ with its positive terminal facing right. The potential at the node between the left battery and the left $2 \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is $V_a - 2$.

The right battery also has an electromotive force of $2 \text{ V}$ with its positive terminal facing right (indicated by the longer line). The potential at the node between the right battery and the right $2 \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is $V_a + 2$.

Let the capacitance of the middle capacitor be $C$. Applying charge conservation for the isolated plates connected to node $b$:

$2(V_b - (V_a - 2)) + 2(V_b - (V_a + 2)) + C(V_b - V_a) = 0$

Substituting $V_b = 0$ yields $2(-V_a + 2) + 2(-V_a - 2) + C(-V_a) = 0$.

$-2V_a + 4 - 2V_a - 4 - CV_a = 0$

$-(4 + C)V_a = 0 \implies V_a = 0$.

Therefore, the potential difference is $V_a - V_b = 0 - 0 = 0$.

305188.subject: Physics
305188.text: An arrangement consists of three conducting concentric spherical shells with radii $a$, $b$, and $c$, as depicted in the figure. The region between the two inner shells is filled by a dielectric of dielectric constant $K$. Determine the capacitance of the system between $A$ and $B$.
options: $\dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K a b c}{K a (c - b) + c(b - a)}$
$\dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 b [K a(c - b) + c(b - a)]}{(b - a)(c - b)}$
$\dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K a b c}{a (c - b) + K c(b - a)}$
$\dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 a b c}{K a (c - b) + c(b - a)}$
305188.sol:
The given arrangement can be considered as two spherical capacitors connected in series.

The first capacitor $C_1$ is formed by the inner shell of radius $a$ and the middle shell of radius $b$. The space between them is filled with a dielectric of constant $K$. Its capacitance is:
$C_1 = \dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K a b}{b - a}$

The second capacitor $C_2$ is formed by the middle shell of radius $b$ and the outer shell of radius $c$. The space between them is vacuum (or air). Its capacitance is:
$C_2 = \dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 b c}{c - b}$

Since the terminals $A$ and $B$ are connected to the innermost and outermost shells respectively, and the middle shell is isolated, the two capacitors are in series. The equivalent capacitance $C_{eq}$ is given by:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{C_1} + \dfrac{1}{C_2}$

Substituting the values of $C_1$ and $C_2$:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{b - a}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K a b} + \dfrac{c - b}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 b c}$

Taking the common denominator:
$\dfrac{1}{C_{eq}} = \dfrac{c(b - a) + K a(c - b)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K a b c}$

Inverting this expression gives the equivalent capacitance:
$C_{eq} = \dfrac{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K a b c}{K a(c - b) + c(b - a)}$

305313.subject: Physics
305313.text: Within a discharge tube filled with a gas, a molecule undergoes ionization, causing an electron to be detached. An electric field of $5.0 \text{ kV m}^{-1}$ is present in the region of the event. Determine the distance travelled by the free electron in $1 \mu\text{s}$, assuming no collisions occur.
305313.sol:
The force experienced by the electron in the electric field is given by $F = eE$.

The acceleration of the electron is $a = \dfrac{eE}{m}$.

Using the equation of motion $s = ut + \dfrac{1}{2}at^2$ with initial velocity $u = 0$, the distance travelled is:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{eE}{m} \right) t^2$

Substituting the standard values $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, $m = 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$, and the given values $E = 5.0 \times 10^3 \text{ V m}^{-1}$, $t = 10^{-6} \text{ s}$:

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 5.0 \times 10^3}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}} \times (10^{-6})^2$

$s = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \dfrac{8.0 \times 10^{-16}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}} \times 10^{-12}$

$s = \dfrac{4.0}{9.1} \times 10^3$

$s = \dfrac{4000}{9.1} \approx 439.56 \text{ m}$

Rounding to the nearest given option, the distance travelled is $440 \text{ m}$.

305336.subject: Physics
305336.text: When $60 \text{ volts}$ are applied across a diode tube, a plate current of $10 \text{ mA}$ is obtained. Assuming that the Langmuir–Child equation $i_p \propto V_p^{3/2}$ is valid, determine the dynamic resistance $r_p$ in this operating condition.
305336.sol:
According to the Langmuir-Child equation, the plate current is given by:

$i_p = k V_p^{3/2}$

Differentiating with respect to $V_p$, we get:

$\dfrac{di_p}{dV_p} = \dfrac{3}{2} k V_p^{1/2}$

Multiplying and dividing by $V_p$ gives:

$\dfrac{di_p}{dV_p} = \dfrac{3}{2} \dfrac{k V_p^{3/2}}{V_p} = \dfrac{3}{2} \dfrac{i_p}{V_p}$

The dynamic resistance $r_p$ is the reciprocal of this derivative:

$r_p = \dfrac{dV_p}{di_p} = \dfrac{2}{3} \dfrac{V_p}{i_p}$

Substituting the given values $V_p = 60 \text{ V}$ and $i_p = 10 \text{ mA} = 10 \times 10^{-3} \text{ A}$:

$r_p = \dfrac{2}{3} \times \dfrac{60}{10 \times 10^{-3}}$

$r_p = \dfrac{2}{3} \times 6000 = 4000 \Omega$

305940.chapter: Magnetic Field due to a Current
305940.text: As shown in the figure, a long wire is bent at its middle to form a right angle. The magnitudes of the magnetic fields at the points $P$, $Q$, $R$, and $S$ are equal. Determine this common magnitude.
305940.sol:
Let the bend of the wire be at the origin $(0,0)$.

The wire consists of two semi-infinite segments:
1. A vertical segment along the negative y-axis.
2. A horizontal segment along the negative x-axis.

The given points are $P(0, -d)$, $Q(d, 0)$, $R(0, d)$, and $S(-d, 0)$.

Consider the magnetic field at point $P(0, -d)$:
Point $P$ lies on the vertical segment, so the magnetic field due to this segment at $P$ is zero.
Point $P$ is at a perpendicular distance $d$ from the end of the semi-infinite horizontal segment.
The magnetic field due to a semi-infinite wire at a perpendicular distance $d$ from its end is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}$.
Thus, the total magnetic field at $P$ is $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}$.

Similarly, point $Q(d, 0)$ lies on the extended axis of the horizontal segment (zero contribution) and is at a perpendicular distance $d$ from the end of the vertical semi-infinite segment. The field at $Q$ is also $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}$.

By symmetry, the fields at $R$ and $S$ have the same magnitude.

The common magnitude is $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}$

306138.subject: Physics
306138.text: The ratio of molar heat capacities for an ideal gas is given as $C_p / C_V = 7/6$. Find the change in internal energy of $1.0$ mole of the gas when its temperature is raised by $50 \text{ K}$ adiabatically.
306138.sol:
Given the ratio of molar heat capacities $\gamma = \dfrac{C_p}{C_V} = \dfrac{7}{6}$

The molar heat capacity at constant volume $C_V$ is given by:

$C_V = \dfrac{R}{\gamma - 1} = \dfrac{R}{\dfrac{7}{6} - 1} = 6R$

The change in internal energy for an ideal gas depends only on the change in temperature and is given by:

$\Delta U = n C_V \Delta T$

Substituting the given values $n = 1.0 \text{ mol}$ and $\Delta T = 50 \text{ K}$:

$\Delta U = 1.0 \times 6R \times 50 = 300R$

Using the universal gas constant $R = 8.3 \text{ J mol}^{-1} \text{ K}^{-1}$:

$\Delta U = 300 \times 8.3 = 2490 \text{ J}$

306366.subject: Physics
306366.text: For tungsten, the wavelength of the $K_\alpha$ X-ray is $21.3 \text{ pm}$. Ejecting an electron from the $L$ shell of a tungsten atom requires $11.3 \text{ keV}$. Determine the minimum accelerating voltage across an X-ray tube equipped with a tungsten target that will permit the emission of $K_\alpha$ X-rays.
306366.sol:
The energy of the emitted $K_\alpha$ X-ray photon is given by:

$E_{K_\alpha} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

Using $hc \approx 1240 \text{ keV pm}$ and $\lambda = 21.3 \text{ pm}$:

$E_{K_\alpha} = \dfrac{1240 \text{ keV pm}}{21.3 \text{ pm}} \approx 58.2 \text{ keV}$

The $K_\alpha$ X-ray is emitted when an electron transitions from the L shell to a vacancy in the K shell. Therefore, the energy difference between the K and L shells is:

$E_{K_\alpha} = E_K - E_L$

Given the binding energy of the L shell $E_L = 11.3 \text{ keV}$, the binding energy of the K shell is:

$E_K = E_{K_\alpha} + E_L = 58.2 \text{ keV} + 11.3 \text{ keV} = 69.5 \text{ keV}$

To permit the emission of $K_\alpha$ X-rays, the incident electrons from the cathode must have sufficient kinetic energy to knock out an electron from the K shell of the tungsten target. Thus, the minimum kinetic energy required is $69.5 \text{ keV}$.

The minimum accelerating voltage $V$ across the X-ray tube is:

$V = \dfrac{E_K}{e} = 69.5 \text{ kV}$

Residents of five States are currently struggling to cope with the effects of intense rainfall. Many of those lucky to have been rescued owe it to the National Disaster Response Force, but such response systems naturally have limited efficacy in predominantly rural States such as Bihar. _______________________________. Capacity-building to handle catastrophic weather events is poor, and serious attention is not given to setting up relief camps, creating crisis-proof health infrastructure and stockpiling dry rations and medicines.
options: In Bihar’s case, the shifting patterns and breaches of the Kosi have added to the complexity of the problem, which requires a deeper understanding of the areas most at risk.
An integrated approach to managing floods requires a sound understanding of the patterns that rivers such as the Ganga and its tributaries display during the monsoon.
What stands out in the annual cycle of floods is the generally tardy pace of preparation for rescue and relief.

Hint:

The sentence preceding the blank states the limited efficacy of our response systems with respect to the flood management and the sentence following the blank validates this constraint by quoting what we actually lack. Clearly, a sentence stating either a limitation or problem would fit the blank.

Among the choices given, the sentence A can be eliminated as it discusses natural limitations instead of those of our response systems.

Besides, while the sentence B seems to be a part of a latter paragraph, the sentence D implies to be opening the current paragraph as it discusses the problem in a broader perspective. Hence, both the options B and D can be eliminated as well.

Sentence E is absolutely absurd in the context and gets eliminated too.

Clearly, option C that contextually fits the blank is the correct answer.

308189.text:
Directions: In these questions, relationship between different elements is shown in the various statements which is followed by three conclusions. Choose the correct answer on the basis of information given below.
Statements: & Y ≥ I > S ,& & H& ≤& A ≤& I ,& & & K > J > A ,& & Z = H < W

Conclusions:& Z < Y,& & & J& ≥ W& ,& & Z = Y
options: Either conclusion I or III follows
Only conclusion III and either conclusion I or II follow
308189.sol:
Statements:& & Y ≥ I > S ,& & H& ≤& A ≤& I ,& & & K > J > A ,& & Z = H < W

Conclusions:& Z < Y,& & & J& ≥ W& ,& & Z = Y

For conclusion I: Z < Y

From statements I, II and IV, we get:

& Y ≥ I ≥ A ≥ H = Z

Here, common sign between Y and Z is ' ≥'. Thus Y ≥ Z or Z ≤ Y.&
Hence conclusion I does not follow individually.

For conclusion II:& J& ≥ W

From statements II, III and IV, we get:

J > A ≥ H < W

Here, we can see that there is opposite sign between J and W, thus no relationship can be established between them.
Hence conclusion II does not follow.

For conclusion III: Z = Y

From statements I, II and IV, we get:

& Y ≥ I ≥ A ≥ H = Z

Here, common sign between Y and Z is ' ≥'. Thus Y ≥ Z or Z ≤ Y.&
Hence conclusion III does not follow individually.

Combining conclusions I and III:

While combining conclusion I i.e. Z < Y and conclusion III i.e. Z = Y, we'll get Z ≤ Y, which is the actual relationship between them.

Therefore, Either conclusion I or conclusion III follows.

Hence option C is correct.

309118.subject: Chemistry
309118.text: Identify the major product of the following reaction:
309118.sol:
Protonation of the terminal alkene by dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ follows Markovnikov's rule, generating a stable tertiary carbocation at the substituted carbon.

The adjacent primary hydroxyl group ($-\text{OH}$) acts as an internal nucleophile, attacking the tertiary carbocation to form a stable 5-membered cyclic ether via intramolecular cyclization.

Deprotonation yields the neutral tetrahydrofuran derivative.

As the starting material has two such alkene and hydroxyl pairs, this cyclization process occurs twice.

The second cyclization forms another 5-membered ring sharing the central quaternary carbon, resulting in a spiro bicyclic compound.

The major product is a spiro compound with two identical oxygen-containing 5-membered rings, matching the structure in option (B).

Answer:

309178.subject: Chemistry
309178.text: Identify the major organic product for the following reaction:
309178.sol:
The given reactant is 2-butanone (ethyl methyl ketone), which has the molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}$.

In the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, aliphatic ketones undergo an acid-catalyzed aldol-type condensation. Specifically, three molecules of the ketone condense to form a substituted benzene ring with the elimination of three molecules of water.

The overall reaction can be represented as:
$3 \text{ C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4} \text{C}_{12}\text{H}_{18} + 3 \text{ H}_2\text{O}$

The product must contain exactly $3 \times 4 = 12$ carbon atoms. Let us check the number of carbon atoms in the given options:
(A) Toluene: $7$ carbon atoms
(B) Pentamethylbenzene: $11$ carbon atoms
(C) 1,3,5-Trimethylbenzene (Mesitylene): $9$ carbon atoms
(D) Hexamethylbenzene: $12$ carbon atoms

Mechanistically, the acid-catalyzed enolization of 2-butanone preferentially forms the more substituted and stable enol, $\text{CH}_3-\text{C(OH)}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$. The nucleophilic attack occurs from the $-\text{CH}_2-$ group (C3) rather than the $-\text{CH}_3$ group (C1).

When three molecules condense, the carbonyl carbon (C2) of one molecule bonds with the $\alpha$-carbon (C3) of the next, forming a six-membered ring of alternating C2 and C3 atoms.
Since C2 is attached to a methyl group (C1) and C3 is attached to a methyl group (C4), every carbon atom in the newly formed benzene ring will have a methyl substituent. This results in the formation of hexamethylbenzene.

309299.subject: Chemistry
309299.text: Which of the following carbohydrates is a non-reducing sugar?
309299.sol:
Reducing sugars are carbohydrates that contain a free aldehyde or ketone group, allowing them to reduce Tollens' or Fehling's reagents. All monosaccharides, including glucose, fructose, and mannose, have a free anomeric carbon and are therefore reducing sugars.

Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by the condensation of $\alpha$-D-glucose and $\beta$-D-fructose. The glycosidic linkage involves the anomeric carbon of glucose (C1) and the anomeric carbon of fructose (C2). Since both anomeric carbons are involved in the bond formation, there is no free aldehyde or ketone group available. Thus, sucrose does not exhibit reducing properties and is classified as a non-reducing sugar.

Answer: Sucrose

309437.subject: Chemistry
309437.text:
Identify the correct order of the ease of decarboxylation for the following three carboxylic acids:

(i)

(ii)

(iii)
309437.sol:
To determine the ease of decarboxylation, we must first identify the type of each carboxylic acid given:

(i) The structure is $CH_2=CH-COOH$, which is an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carboxylic acid.
(ii) The structure is $CH_3-CH=CH-CH_2-COOH$, which is a $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated carboxylic acid.
(iii) The structure is $CH_3-CO-CH_2-COOH$, which is a $\beta$-keto carboxylic acid.

Now, let us compare their mechanisms for decarboxylation upon heating:

1. $\beta$-keto acids (iii) undergo decarboxylation very easily (even at mild temperatures like $50^{}^{{}^{\circ}}\text{C}$) via a stable six-membered cyclic transition state. The carbonyl oxygen strongly hydrogen-bonds with the acidic proton, facilitating the cleavage of the $C-C$ bond to release $CO_2$ and form an enol, which rapidly tautomerizes to a ketone.

2. $\beta,\gamma$-unsaturated acids (ii) also undergo decarboxylation via a similar six-membered cyclic transition state, where the $\pi$-bond acts as the proton acceptor. However, because a $C=C\pi$-bond is a weaker hydrogen bond acceptor than a $C=O$ oxygen, the transition state is less stable than that of a $\beta$-keto acid. Thus, it requires higher temperatures to decarboxylate compared to (iii).

3. $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated acids (i) cannot form such a six-membered cyclic transition state. Their decarboxylation would require the formation of a highly unstable vinylic carbanion intermediate, making the process very difficult and requiring much harsher conditions.

Therefore, the correct order for the ease of decarboxylation is $\text{(iii)} > \text{(ii)} > \text{(i)}$.

Answer: $\text{(iii)} > \text{(ii)} > \text{(i)}$

(III)
309476.sol:
The reactivity of carbonyl compounds towards nucleophilic addition (such as reduction by $\mathrm{NaBH}_{4}$) depends on the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon and steric hindrance.

Compound (I) is formaldehyde ($\mathrm{HCHO}$), (II) is acetaldehyde ($\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$), and (III) is N,N-dimethylacetamide ($\mathrm{CH_3CON(CH_3)_2}$).

$\mathrm{NaBH}_{4}$ is a mild reducing agent that readily reduces aldehydes and ketones but does not reduce amides. Thus, the amide (III) is the least reactive.

Comparing the aldehydes, the methyl group in acetaldehyde (II) exerts an electron-donating +I effect, which decreases the magnitude of the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon. It also increases steric hindrance compared to the hydrogen atoms in formaldehyde (I).

Therefore, formaldehyde (I) is more reactive than acetaldehyde (II).

The decreasing order of reactivity is (I) > (II) > (III).

Answer: (I) > (II) > (III)

309612.subject: Chemistry
309612.text:
Which of the following molecules are chiral?

(i)
(ii)
(iii)
309612.sol:
To determine if a molecule is chiral, we need to check for the presence of a plane of symmetry (POS) or a center of symmetry (COS). Molecules lacking both (and more generally, any alternating axis of symmetry $S_n$) are chiral.

1. Molecule (i) is trans-1,2-dimethylcyclobutane. One methyl group is pointing towards the viewer (wedge) and the other is pointing away (dash). This molecule lacks both a plane of symmetry and a center of symmetry. It only possesses a $C_2$ axis of symmetry. Therefore, it is a chiral molecule and exists as a pair of enantiomers.

2. Molecule (ii) is 1,3-dimethylcyclobutane. Regardless of its specific stereochemistry (cis or trans), it is achiral due to the presence of a plane of symmetry:
- In cis-1,3-dimethylcyclobutane (both methyls on the same side), there is a plane of symmetry passing through the C2 and C4 atoms.
- In trans-1,3-dimethylcyclobutane (one methyl up, one down), there is a plane of symmetry passing through the C1 and C3 atoms.
Thus, molecule (ii) is achiral.

3. Molecule (iii) is cis-1-chloro-2-methylcyclobutane. Both substituents are on the same side of the ring (wedged). If both substituents were identical, there would be a plane of symmetry bisecting the C1-C2 bond. However, because the substituents are different ($-$Cl and $-$CH_3$), this plane of symmetry is broken. It also lacks a center of symmetry. Therefore, molecule (iii) is chiral.

Since molecules (i) and (iii) are chiral, the correct option is (A).

Answer: (i) and (iii)$

309638.subject: Chemistry
309638.text:
Identify the correct order of stability for the following quinones:

I.

II.

III.
309638.sol:
The given compounds are:
I. p-benzoquinone
II. o-benzoquinone
III. diphenoquinone

In p-benzoquinone (I), the two carbonyl groups are at the para position. Their dipoles are directed opposite to each other, which minimizes dipole-dipole repulsion, making it quite stable.

In o-benzoquinone (II), the two carbonyl groups are adjacent (ortho position). This causes strong dipole-dipole repulsion, making it highly unstable and reactive.

In diphenoquinone (III), there are two quinonoid rings. The formation of this structure involves the loss of aromaticity of two benzene rings, whereas p-benzoquinone involves the loss of aromaticity of only one benzene ring. Because of this greater loss of aromatic resonance energy, diphenoquinone is thermodynamically less stable than p-benzoquinone.

However, diphenoquinone (III) benefits from extended conjugation and does not suffer from the severe adjacent dipole-dipole repulsion seen in o-benzoquinone (II). Thus, it is more stable than o-benzoquinone.

Combining these factors, the correct order of stability is $\text{I} > \text{III} > \text{II}$.

Answer: $\text{I} > \text{III} > \text{II}$

The formula to calculate the mass of the Earth considering it a sphere is given by

$M = \dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}d . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the time period of revolution of the satellite can be written as

$T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R3}{GM}} . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the expression for the mass from equation (1) into equation (2) and simplify to obtain the expression for the required quantity.

$\begin{cases}T & = & 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R3}{G\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3}d}} \\ & = & 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{4\piGd}} \\ & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{12{π}^{2}}{4\piGd}} \\ & = & \sqrt{\dfrac{3\pi}{Gd}} \\ & ⇒ & \dfrac{3\pi}{Gd} = T^{2}\end{cases}$

314743.text: Let ABC be an isosceles triangle with $\mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{BC}$. A trisector of $\angle \mathrm{B}$ meets AC at D . If $\mathrm{AB}, \mathrm{AC}$ and $B D$ are integers and $A B-B D=3$, find $A C$.
314743.sol: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{I_1}{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right)}=\frac{I_3}{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-3 \theta\right)} \\ & \Rightarrow \text { put } I_3=I_1-3 \\ & \Rightarrow I_1=\frac{3}{4} \operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta \\ & \text { If } \operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta=36 \\ & \text { i.e. } \operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta=6\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} & \text { i.e. } \sin \theta=\frac{1}{6} \\ & I_1=\frac{3}{4} \times 36=27 \\ & I_3=24 \\ & \frac{I_1}{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)}=\frac{D C}{\sin 4 \theta} \& \frac{I_1}{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\theta\right)}=\frac{A D}{\sin 2 \theta} \\ & \Rightarrow I_2=\frac{I_1 \sin 4 \theta}{\cos \theta}+\frac{I_1 \sin 2 \theta}{\cos \theta} \\ & \Rightarrow I_2=I_1 \times 2 \times \sin 3 \theta\end{aligned}$ $\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & \frac{3}{4} \operatorname{cosec}^2 \theta \times 2 \times \sin 3 \theta \\ \Rightarrow & \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{3}{\sin \theta}-4 \sin \theta\right) \\ \mathrm{I}_2 & =\frac{3}{2}\left(3 \times 6-\frac{4}{6}\right) \\ & =\frac{3}{2}\left(18-\frac{2}{3}\right) \\ & =\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{54-2}{3}\right) \\ & =\frac{3}{2} \times \frac{52}{3} \\ \mathrm{I}_2 & =26\end{aligned}$

69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5b177.text: Pure water can be obtained from seawater by _____.
69b2e1a6db9e5a9e03d5b177.sol:
When the external pressure, greater than the osmotic pressure, is applied on a solution separated by semipermeable membrane, the transfer of solvent particles take place from higher concentration to lower concentration. This phenomenon is known as reverse osmosis.

So, the seawater can be converted to pure water by reverse osmosis.

6a1bb6bc107bf677676d9f1f.subject: Physics
6a1bb6bc107bf677676d9f1f.text: An ideal gas is compressed from a common initial state $I$ to a final volume $V_f$ via three different processes as shown in the $P-V$ diagram. The processes are known to be isothermal, adiabatic, and isobaric. Which curve correctly represents the adiabatic compression?
options: Either Curve 1 or 2 depending on the atomicity of the gas
6a1bb6bc107bf677676d9f1f.sol:
For an ideal gas, the equations for the given processes are:
Isobaric: $P = \text{constant}$
Isothermal: $PV = \text{constant}$
Adiabatic: $PV^\gamma = \text{constant}$

Curve 3 is a horizontal line ($P = \text{constant}$), so it represents the isobaric process.

The slope of the $P-V$ curve is given by $\dfrac{dP}{dV}$.
For an isothermal process: $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\dfrac{P}{V}$
For an adiabatic process: $\dfrac{dP}{dV} = -\gamma \dfrac{P}{V}$

Since the heat capacity ratio $\gamma > 1$, the magnitude of the slope for the adiabatic curve is greater than that for the isothermal curve. This means the adiabatic curve is steeper.

During compression, the volume decreases. Starting from a common initial state $I$, the steeper curve will rise to a higher final pressure for the same final volume $V_f$.

From the given graph, at $V = V_f$, the pressure for Curve 1 is greater than the pressure for Curve 2. Therefore, Curve 1 represents the adiabatic compression and Curve 2 represents the isothermal compression.

Answer: Curve 1

6a2109b0219e1ae5a172295e.subject: Chemistry
6a2109b0219e1ae5a172295e.text:
Determine the total number of geometrical isomers possible for the following two polyenes:
(I) $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH-CH=CH-CH=CH-CH_3}$
(II) $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH-CH=CH-C_6H_5}$
6a2109b0219e1ae5a172295e.sol:
For compound (I): $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH-CH=CH-CH=CH-CH_3}$

The number of double bonds capable of showing geometrical isomerism is $n = 3$.

Since the terminal groups are different ($\mathrm{C_6H_5}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3}$), the molecule is unsymmetrical.

The number of geometrical isomers is given by $2^n$.

Substituting $n = 3$, the number of geometrical isomers is $2^3 = 8$.

For compound (II): $\mathrm{C_6H_5-CH=CH-CH=CH-C_6H_5}$

The number of double bonds capable of showing geometrical isomerism is $n = 2$.

Since the terminal groups are identical ($\mathrm{C_6H_5}$), the molecule is symmetrical.

For a symmetrical polyene with an even number of double bonds, the number of geometrical isomers is given by $2^{n-1} + 2^{(n/2)-1}$.

Substituting $n = 2$, the number of geometrical isomers is $2^{2-1} + 2^{(2/2)-1} = 2^1 + 2^0 = 2 + 1 = 3$.

The total number of geometrical isomers for (I) and (II) are 8 and 3 respectively.

Answer: 8 and 3

6a2109b3219e1ae5a17229b9.subject: Biology
6a2109b3219e1ae5a17229b9.text:
Read the following statements with reference to lipids:
(a) Lecithin is a phosphorylated organic compound found in cell membranes.
(b) Arachidonic acid contains $20$ carbon atoms excluding the carboxyl carbon.
(c) Gingelly oil has a higher melting point and remains solid in winters.
(d) Lipids found in neural tissues have more complex structures.
(e) Triglycerides are formed by the esterification of three glycerol molecules with one fatty acid molecule.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
6a2109b3219e1ae5a17229b9.sol:
Statement (a) is correct. Lecithin is a phospholipid, which contains phosphorus and a phosphorylated organic compound, and is found in cell membranes.

Statement (b) is incorrect. Arachidonic acid contains $20$ carbon atoms including the carboxyl carbon.

Statement (c) is incorrect. Gingelly oil has a lower melting point and hence remains as oil in winters.

Statement (d) is correct. Lipids found in neural tissues have more complex structures, such as sphingolipids and gangliosides.

Statement (e) is incorrect. Triglycerides are formed by the esterification of one glycerol molecule with three fatty acid molecules.

Therefore, only statements (a) and (d) are correct.

Answer: (a) and (d) only

6a2a77bdfad2360f42564b9e.text: For a convex lens, if an incident ray of light passes through its first principal focus before striking the lens, the refracted ray will :
options: pass through the second principal focus on the other side of the lens.
emerge parallel to the principal axis.
pass undeviated through the optical centre of the lens.
retrace its path back along the same line.
6a2a77bdfad2360f42564b9e.sol:
According to the rules of image formation by a convex lens, an incident ray of light passing through the first principal focus of the lens becomes parallel to the principal axis after refraction.

This is based on the principle of reversibility of light, as a ray parallel to the principal axis passes through the principal focus after refraction.

Answer: emerge parallel to the principal axis.

6a0e2775165ae1327797b372.subject: Physics
6a0e2775165ae1327797b372.text: A particle moves along a straight line such that the time $t$ and position $x$ are related by the equation $t = 3x^2 - 4x$. If $v$ represents the instantaneous velocity of the particle, which of the following expressions gives its acceleration?
6a0e2775165ae1327797b372.sol:
Given $t = 3x^2 - 4x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 6x - 4$

The instantaneous velocity $v$ is given by:

$v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{6x - 4}$

The acceleration $a$ is given by:

$a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = v \dfrac{dv}{dx}$

Differentiating $v$ with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx} (6x - 4)^{-1} = -1(6x - 4)^{-2} \times 6 = -6(6x - 4)^{-2}$

Since $v = (6x - 4)^{-1}$, we have $(6x - 4)^{-2} = v^2$

$\dfrac{dv}{dx} = -6v^2$

Substituting this into the expression for acceleration:

$a = v(-6v^2) = -6v^3$

Answer: $-6v^3$

6a16f3277cfacf7984f86706.text:
Consider the following sequence of reactions:

Identify the major product 'Z'.
6a16f3277cfacf7984f86706.sol:
The reaction of 2-methylpropene with HBr in the presence of peroxide follows anti-Markovnikov's rule (Kharasch effect) to give 1-bromo-2-methylpropane (X).

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{CH}_2 + \text{HBr} \xrightarrow{\text{Peroxide}} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ (X)

1-Bromo-2-methylpropane reacts with magnesium in dry ether to form the corresponding Grignard reagent, isobutylmagnesium bromide (Y).

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{Mg} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{MgBr}$ (Y)

The Grignard reagent (Y) undergoes nucleophilic addition with formaldehyde (HCHO) followed by acidic hydrolysis to yield a primary alcohol with one additional carbon atom.

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{MgBr} + \text{HCHO} \rightarrow (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OMgBr}$

$(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OMgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$ (Z)

The final product Z is 3-methylbu\tan^{-1}-ol.

Answer: 3-Methylbu\tan^{-1}-ol

6a2109b0219e1ae5a1722969.subject: Chemistry
6a2109b0219e1ae5a1722969.text: In which of the following arrangements is the given sequence not strictly according to the property indicated against it?
options: $H_2O > H_2S > H_2Se > H_2Te :$ Decreasing bond angle
$NH_3 < PH_3 < AsH_3 < SbH_3 :$ Increasing thermal stability
$HClO < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4 :$ Increasing acidic strength
$HF < HCl < HBr < HI :$ Increasing reducing character
6a2109b0219e1ae5a1722969.sol:
The thermal stability of hydrides of Group 15 elements decreases down the group. This is because the size of the central atom increases down the group, which leads to an increase in the M-H bond length and a corresponding decrease in the bond dissociation enthalpy.

Therefore, the correct order of thermal stability is $NH_3 > PH_3 > AsH_3 > SbH_3$.

The given sequence $NH_3 < PH_3 < AsH_3 < SbH_3$ represents decreasing thermal stability, not increasing. Hence, this arrangement is not strictly according to the property indicated.

For the other options:
The bond angle of Group 16 hydrides decreases down the group due to decreasing electronegativity of the central atom ($H_2O > H_2S > H_2Se > H_2Te$).
The acidic strength of oxoacids of chlorine increases with the oxidation state of chlorine ($HClO < HClO_2 < HClO_3 < HClO_4$).
The reducing character of hydrogen halides increases down the group as the H-X bond strength decreases ($HF < HCl < HBr < HI$).

Answer: $NH_3 < PH_3 < AsH_3 < SbH_3 :$ Increasing thermal stability

Match List I with List II.

List IList II
A$[CoF_6]^{3-}$1$1.73\text{ BM}$
B$[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$2$4.90\text{ BM}$
C$[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$3$0\text{ BM}$
D$[Zn(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$4$2.83\text{ BM}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
6a2109b0219e1ae5a172296a.sol:
For $[CoF_6]^{3-}$, $Co$ is in $+3$ oxidation state. $Co^{3+}$ has $3d^6$ configuration. Since $F^-$ is a weak field ligand, it forms a high spin complex with $4$ unpaired electrons. $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90 \text{ BM}$.

For $[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}$, $Ni$ is in $+2$ oxidation state. $Ni^{2+}$ has $3d^8$ configuration. It has $2$ unpaired electrons. $\mu = \sqrt{2(2+2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83 \text{ BM}$.

For $[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, $Cu$ is in $+2$ oxidation state. $Cu^{2+}$ has $3d^9$ configuration. It has $1$ unpaired electron. $\mu = \sqrt{1(1+2)} = \sqrt{3} \approx 1.73 \text{ BM}$.

For $[Zn(NH_3)_4]^{2+}$, $Zn$ is in $+2$ oxidation state. $Zn^{2+}$ has $3d^{10}$ configuration. It has $0$ unpaired electrons. $\mu = 0 \text{ BM}$.

Thus, the correct matching is A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3.

Answer: A-2, B-4, C-1, D-3

6a7a1ff8690eaf2104a0e2bc.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8690eaf2104a0e2bc.text:
The electric potential at a point due to a point charge at a distance of $45 \text{ cm}$ is $-40 \text{ V}$. The value of the point charge is:
(Assume $\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 9 \times 10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}$)
6a7a1ff8690eaf2104a0e2bc.sol:
The electric potential due to a point charge is given by

$V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \dfrac{Q}{r}$

Given data:
$V = -40 \text{ V}$
$r = 45 \text{ cm} = 0.45 \text{ m}$

Rearranging the formula to solve for the charge $Q$:

$Q = \dfrac{V \cdot r}{\dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}}$

Substituting the values:

$Q = \dfrac{-40 \times 0.45}{9 \times 10^9}$

$Q = \dfrac{-18}{9 \times 10^9}$

$Q = -2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ C}$

$Q = -2 \text{ nC}$

Answer: $-2 \text{ nC}$

6a7a1ff8b288d8d6cd34bea8.text: A block is projected upwards along a rough inclined plane of angle $45^{\circ}$. If the retardation of the block is $g$, the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the plane is
6a7a1ff8b288d8d6cd34bea8.sol:
When the block moves up the incline, both the component of gravity and kinetic friction act downwards along the plane.

The equation of motion is:
$ma = mg \sin 45^{\circ} + \mu_k mg \cos 45^{\circ}$

Given that retardation $a = g$:
$g = g \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \right) + \mu_k g \left( \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \right)$

$1 = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \dfrac{\mu_k}{\sqrt{2}}$

$\sqrt{2} = 1 + \mu_k$

$\mu_k = \sqrt{2} - 1$

Answer: $\sqrt{2}-1$

6a7a1ff82aecdb6619fa0176.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff82aecdb6619fa0176.text: A solid sphere and a hollow sphere of the same mass have the same radius of gyration about their respective diametric axes. If the ratio of the radius of the solid sphere to the radius of the hollow sphere is $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3}}$, then the value of $x$ is _______.
6a7a1ff82aecdb6619fa0176.sol:
Let the mass of both spheres be $m$.

The moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its diameter is $I_1 = \dfrac{2}{5}mR_1^2$, so its radius of gyration is $k_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R_1$.

The moment of inertia of the hollow sphere about its diameter is $I_2 = \dfrac{2}{3}mR_2^2$, so its radius of gyration is $k_2 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R_2$.

Given that $k_1 = k_2$, we have:
$\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{3}}R_2$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{5}{3}}$

Comparing this with the given ratio $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{3}}$, we get $x = 5$.

Answer: $5$

6a7a1ff8db8b1d53c5156a6d.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8db8b1d53c5156a6d.text: A uniform ladder rests against a perfectly smooth vertical wall and a rough horizontal floor. It makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal floor and is on the verge of slipping. The minimum coefficient of static friction $\mu$ between the ladder and the floor is :
6a7a1ff8db8b1d53c5156a6d.sol:
Let the weight of the ladder be $W$ and its length be $L$.

For translational equilibrium, the normal reaction from the floor $N_{f}$ balances the weight of the ladder:
$N_{f} = W$

The normal reaction from the wall $N_{w}$ balances the static friction $f$ from the floor:
$f = N_{w}$

For rotational equilibrium, taking torque about the point of contact with the floor:
The weight $W$ acts at the center of the ladder, producing a torque $W \left( \dfrac{L}{2} \cos \theta \right)$.
The normal reaction from the wall $N_{w}$ produces an opposing torque $N_{w} (L \sin \theta)$.

Equating the torques:
$W \left( \dfrac{L}{2} \cos \theta \right) = N_{w} (L \sin \theta)$
$\Rightarrow N_{w} = \dfrac{W}{2} \cot \theta$

Since the ladder is on the verge of slipping, the friction is limiting:
$f = \mu N_{f}$

Substituting $f = N_{w}$ and $N_{f} = W$:
$\dfrac{W}{2} \cot \theta = \mu W$
$\Rightarrow \mu = \dfrac{1}{2} \cot \theta$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2} \cot \theta$

6a7a1ff89be4d528ff15d185.text: Two solid spheres $A$ and $B$, made of the same material, are falling through a long column of a viscous liquid. The ratio of the radius of sphere $A$ to that of sphere $B$ is $1:2$. When both spheres have attained their respective terminal velocities, the ratio of the rate of heat generation (viscous power dissipation) of sphere $A$ to that of sphere $B$ is
6a7a1ff89be4d528ff15d185.sol:
The rate of heat generation (power dissipated) by viscous drag is given by $P = F_v \cdot v_t$.

According to Stokes' law, the viscous drag force is $F_v = 6\pi\eta r v_t$.
Thus, $P = (6\pi\eta r v_t) \cdot v_t = 6\pi\eta r v_t^2$.

The terminal velocity of a sphere falling in a viscous fluid is given by $v_t = \dfrac{2r^2g(\rho_s - \rho_l)}{9\eta}$.
For spheres of the same material in the same liquid, $v_t \propto r^2$.

Substituting the proportionality of $v_t$ into the power equation:
$P \propto r(r^2)^2$
$P \propto r^5$

Given the ratio of radii is $r_A : r_B = 1:2$, the ratio of power dissipation is:
$\dfrac{P_A}{P_B} = \left(\dfrac{r_A}{r_B}\right)^5 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^5 = \dfrac{1}{32}$.

Therefore, the ratio is $1:32$.

Answer: $1:32$

6a7a1ff8af7a0cf0763e3e26.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff8af7a0cf0763e3e26.text: A particle executes simple harmonic motion. Which of the following describes the graph showing the variation of its potential energy ($PE$) with the magnitude of its velocity ($v$) as it moves from the extreme position to the mean position?
options: A downward-opening parabola with its vertex on the positive $PE$ axis
An upward-opening parabola passing through the origin
A straight line with a negative slope
A straight line passing through the origin with a positive slope
6a7a1ff8af7a0cf0763e3e26.sol:
The potential energy ($PE$) of a particle in SHM is given by $PE = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2x^2$.

The velocity $v$ of the particle is related to its displacement $x$ by the equation $v^2 = \omega^2(A^2 - x^2)$, where $A$ is the amplitude.

Rearranging this for $x^2$, we get $x^2 = A^2 - \dfrac{v^2}{\omega^2}$.

Substituting this into the potential energy equation:
$PE = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2\left(A^2 - \dfrac{v^2}{\omega^2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}m\omega^2A^2 - \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2$

This equation is of the form $y = -cx^2 + k$ (where $c$ and $k$ are positive constants). This represents a downward-opening parabola with its maximum value (vertex) at $v = 0$ on the positive $PE$ axis.

Answer: A downward-opening parabola with its vertex on the positive $PE$ axis

6a7a1ff8991b4cc93ec44c0c.text: A long straight solid cylindrical conductor of radius $R$ carries a steady current uniformly distributed over its cross-section. The magnitude of the magnetic field at a radial distance $x$ (where $x < R$) is found to be equal to the magnitude of the magnetic field at a radial distance $y$ (where $y > R$). Which of the following relations is correct?
6a7a1ff8991b4cc93ec44c0c.sol:
For a solid cylindrical conductor carrying a uniform current $I$, the magnetic field at a distance $r$ from the axis is given by:

Inside the conductor ($r < R$):
$B_{\text{in}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}$

Outside the conductor ($r > R$):
$B_{\text{out}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$

Given that the magnetic field at distance $x$ ($x < R$) is equal to the magnetic field at distance $y$ ($y > R$), we can equate the two expressions:

$\dfrac{\mu_0 I x}{2\pi R^2} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi y}$

Cancelling the common terms $\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi}$ from both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{x}{R^2} = \dfrac{1}{y}$

Rearranging the terms yields:

$xy = R^2$

Answer: $xy = R^2$

6a7a1ff86d0e167a71109e85.subject: Physics
6a7a1ff86d0e167a71109e85.text: A hydrogen atom of mass $m$, initially at rest in an excited state with principal quantum number $n$, transitions to the ground state. It emits a photon and recoils with a speed $v$. If $R$ is the Rydberg constant and $h$ is Planck's constant, the value of $n$ is :
6a7a1ff86d0e167a71109e85.sol:
By the principle of conservation of linear momentum, the recoil momentum of the hydrogen atom must be equal in magnitude to the momentum of the emitted photon.

$p_{\text{atom}} = p_{\text{photon}}$

$mv = \dfrac{h}{\lambda}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\lambda} = \dfrac{mv}{h}$

Using the Rydberg formula for the hydrogen atom ($Z=1$) transitioning from state $n$ to the ground state ($n_f = 1$):

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left(\dfrac{1}{1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n^2}\right)$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{1}{\lambda}$:

$\dfrac{mv}{h} = R \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{n^2}\right)$

$\dfrac{mv}{hR} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{n^2}$

$\dfrac{1}{n^2} = 1 - \dfrac{mv}{hR} = \dfrac{hR - mv}{hR}$

Taking the reciprocal and the square root:

$n = \sqrt{\dfrac{hR}{hR - mv}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{hR}{hR - mv}}$

6a7a1ff81264c2f8513f0f03.subject: Chemistry
6a7a1ff81264c2f8513f0f03.text: An acid-base reaction proceeds predominantly in the direction that forms the weaker acid and the weaker base. Based on this principle, which of the following reactions is thermodynamically feasible in the forward direction?
6a7a1ff81264c2f8513f0f03.sol:
For an acid-base equilibrium to be favored in the forward direction, the reactant acid must be stronger than the product acid. We compare the acidity of the hydrocarbons based on the hybridization of the carbon atom holding the acidic proton ($sp > sp^2 > sp^3$).

In the first option, the reactant acid is ethene ($sp^2$) and the product acid is ethyne ($sp$). Since ethyne is a stronger acid than ethene, the backward reaction is favored.

In the second option, the reactant acid is propyne ($sp$) and the product acid is ethane ($sp^3$). Since propyne is a stronger acid than ethane, the forward reaction is thermodynamically feasible.

In the third option, the reactant acid is ethane ($sp^3$) and the product acid is ammonia. Ammonia is a stronger acid than alkanes, so the backward reaction is favored.

In the fourth option, the reactant acid is benzene ($sp^2$) and the product acid is propyne ($sp$). Since propyne is a stronger acid than benzene, the backward reaction is favored.

Answer: $CH_3-C\equiv CH + CH_3CH_2^{-}Na^{+} \rightarrow CH_3-C\equiv C^{-}Na^{+} + CH_3CH_3$

6a7a1ff8bf20203a5e0e4f80.text: Complete combustion of $1.8\text{ g}$ of an oxygen-containing organic compound gave $2.64\text{ g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ and $1.08\text{ g}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. If the vapour density of the compound is $30$, the total number of atoms present in one molecule of the compound is
6a7a1ff8bf20203a5e0e4f80.sol:
Mass of carbon in the compound = $\dfrac{12}{44} \times \text{Mass of CO}_2 = \dfrac{12}{44} \times 2.64 = 0.72\text{ g}$

Mass of hydrogen in the compound = $\dfrac{2}{18} \times \text{Mass of H}_2\text{O} = \dfrac{2}{18} \times 1.08 = 0.12\text{ g}$

Mass of oxygen in the compound = Total mass - (Mass of C + Mass of H)
Mass of oxygen = $1.8 - (0.72 + 0.12) = 1.8 - 0.84 = 0.96\text{ g}$

Moles of C = $\dfrac{0.72}{12} = 0.06\text{ mol}$
Moles of H = $\dfrac{0.12}{1} = 0.12\text{ mol}$
Moles of O = $\dfrac{0.96}{16} = 0.06\text{ mol}$

The molar ratio of C : H : O is $0.06 : 0.12 : 0.06$, which simplifies to $1 : 2 : 1$.
The empirical formula is $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$.
Empirical formula mass = $12 + 2(1) + 16 = 30$

Molar mass of the compound = $2 \times \text{Vapour density} = 2 \times 30 = 60$

Multiplying factor $n = \dfrac{\text{Molar mass}}{\text{Empirical formula mass}} = \dfrac{60}{30} = 2$

Molecular formula = $(\text{CH}_2\text{O})_2 = \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$

Total number of atoms in one molecule = $2 + 4 + 2 = 8$

Answer: $8$
